rationale: The decision directly concerns Dutch water law and regional water authority governance: provincial approval under the Waterwet of the dike reinforcement project plan ("Waterwet Versterking Markermeerdijken") adopted by Hoogheemraadschap Hollands Noorderkwartier. Dike reinforcement project plans by waterboards fall squarely under waterboard_governance and are substantively WATER under both labels.

This Dutch College van Beroep voor het bedrijfsleven (CBb) decision concerns an administrative fine for exceeding animal manure application standards (mestboete / gebruiksnorm dierlijke meststoffen) and the revocation of an agricultural manure derogation permit (intrekking derogatievergunning) under Dutch manure legislation (Meststoffenwet). Under the protocol rules, agricultural manure and phosphate regulatory disputes are NOT_WATER and fall under not_water_related.

This Dutch College van Beroep voor het bedrijfsleven (CBb) decision concerns agricultural phosphate quotas (fosfaatrechten) and an exemption (ontheffing) for dairy cattle manure production under the Meststoffenwet (Fertilizers Act), which the protocol explicitly classifies as NOT_WATER rather than water law or water governance.

This Dutch Trade and Industry Appeals Tribunal (CBb) decision concerns a cross-compliance subsidy reduction (randvoorwaardenkorting) imposed on a dairy farm for exceeding animal manure and phosphate application standards under the Dutch Fertilizers Act (Meststoffenwet) in 2015, along with limitation-period rules under Regulation 2988/95. Under the coding protocol, agricultural manure and phosphate quota/standard disputes under the Meststoffenwet are explicitly NOT_WATER and categorized as not_water_related.

The decision concerns an administrative fine imposed on a transporter of animal manure under the Dutch Meststoffenwet (Fertilizers Act) and procedural defences regarding evidence disclosure and fair trial principles. Under the protocol rules, Meststoffenwet agricultural manure disputes are explicitly classified as NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

The Dutch administrative decision directly adjudicates an appeal against the refusal ('Weigering') of a water permit ('Watervergunning') under the regional water authority ordinance ('Keur Amstel, Gooi en Vecht'). Under the protocol, decisions concerning a Watervergunning and waterschap Keur are substantively WATER under both labels and best classified under regulatory_permit (with waterboard_governance context), with no household utility connection or informal settlement issue.

This Dutch administrative court decision (RBMNE) explicitly concerns a permit granted under the Dutch Water Act ('Vergunning op grond van de Waterwet'), adjudicating whether the claimants qualify as interested parties ('belanghebbende') experiencing consequences of any significance at their parcel. Per the protocol, an explicit Waterwet permit challenge is substantively WATER under both labels and falls squarely within 'regulatory_permit'.

The decision directly adjudicates appeals by both an industrial discharger and drinking water utilities against a permit granted under the Dutch Water Act (Waterwet) setting tightened discharge standards (lozingsnormen) and monitoring obligations for pyrazole in treated wastewater discharged into a water system. It is squarely a water regulatory/discharge permit dispute (regulatory_permit) with no household service connection or informal settlement dimension.

This CBb decision concerns a Common Agricultural Policy cross-compliance subsidy reduction (Randvoorwaardenkorting) under Article 5 of the Dutch Fertilizer/Manure Use Decree (Besluit gebruik meststoffen). Agricultural manure regulation and farm subsidy compliance penalties are governed by agricultural/manure law rather than substantive water law or water governance.

Dutch College van Beroep voor het bedrijfsleven (CBb) decision concerning a CAP cross-compliance subsidy reduction (randvoorwaardenkorting) for failure to apply animal manure using low-emission methods (emissiearm aanwenden dierlijke meststoffen). Under the coding protocol, agricultural manure/fertilizer compliance disputes under Dutch manure regulations are NOT_WATER.

The dispute concerns tailor-made environmental regulations (maatwerkvoorschriften under the Activiteitenbesluit milieubeheer) imposed on a manure/fertilizer pellet processing facility in Helmond due to excessive odour nuisance (geurhinder). Under the coding protocol, manure processing and odour nuisance permits without a substantive water governance or water infrastructure dispute are classified as NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

This Dutch College van Beroep voor het bedrijfsleven (CBb) decision concerns administrative fines imposed under the Meststoffenwet (Fertilizers Act) on a transport company carrying animal manure, addressing procedural defense rights, administrative reports, and fine calculation. Under the protocol rules, Meststoffenwet animal manure regulation/fines without substantive water law or water governance issues are classified as NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

The Dutch administrative court summary explicitly identifies the dispute subject matter as 'watervergunning' (a statutory water permit under the Dutch Waterwet), which under the coding protocol is substantively WATER and falls squarely within the regulatory_permit governance category.

This Dutch Council of State (RvS) decision concerns a claim for administrative loss compensation (nadeelcompensatie) brought by the regional water board (Wetterskip Fryslân) against the Province of Fryslân for approximately €800,000 in costs incurred relocating wastewater transport pipelines (transportleidingen voor afvalwater) due to provincial infrastructure works. Because the dispute directly governs wastewater infrastructure operated by a water board and the allocation of costs for relocating sewage/wastewater trunk lines, it is substantively about water/wastewater infrastructure (WATER under both labels) and best fits sanitation_sewage, without involving household connection refusal or informal settlements.

The summary explicitly identifies the dispute as an appeal concerning a permit granted under the Dutch Water Act ('vergunning op grond van de Waterwet; beroep ongegrond'), which per the coding protocol is substantively WATER and falls squarely under regulatory_permit.

This Dutch preliminary injunction (voorlopige voorziening / vovo) challenges a granted water permit (watervergunning) alongside an environmental/planning permit (omgevingsvergunning) and traffic decision for constructing a bicycle bridge, bicycle path and bypass. Under the protocol rules, a challenge to a Waterwet/watervergunning permit is substantively WATER under both labels and falls within regulatory_permit, with no household water connection refusal or informal settlement issue.

The decision concerns administrative enforcement (last onder dwangsom) against the holding company of a bankrupt butcher shop for violating Article 6.2(1) of the Dutch Waterwet, which prohibits discharging substances into surface water bodies without a water permit (watervergunning). It directly adjudicates statutory water discharge regulation under the Waterwet and does not involve household service connection or informal settlements.

This Dutch Raad van State decision concerns a provincial administrative enforcement order (last onder bestuursdwang) following a fire (ongewoon voorval) in a pile of solid commercial waste at a waste-processing facility, requiring removal of burned solid waste and suspending acceptance of new solid waste until compliant floor storage is ensured and incoming waste cannot contaminate wastewater present on site (such as pooled firefighting water). The primary dispute involves solid-waste facility fire remediation under general environmental law rather than water law, water governance, wastewater discharge permitting, or water utility services.

The decision concerns an administrative fine imposed under the Dutch Fertilizers Act (Meststoffenwet) on an intermediary transporter for failing to draw up animal manure transport certificates (vervoersbewijs dierlijke meststoffen) and comply with related Meststoffenwet obligations when hauling sawdust/manure loads from a slaughterhouse. Per the protocol rules, regulatory disputes under the Meststoffenwet without substantive water law or water governance adjudication are classified as NOT_WATER.

This Dutch administrative decision (Rechtbank Den Haag) concerns an administrative enforcement order with penalty payments (last onder dwangsom) regarding the discharge (lozing) of industrial PFAS chemicals (APFO/PFOA). In Dutch environmental and water law, 'lozing' specifically denotes wastewater/effluent discharge into surface water, sewer infrastructure, or soil/groundwater. Because the dispute centers on enforcement against industrial chemical effluent pollution, both labels are WATER and the primary governance category is environmental_protection.

This CBb appeal concerns administrative fines imposed on an agricultural partnership for exceeding animal manure, nitrogen and phosphate application standards, failing to meet manure processing obligations (mestverwerkingsplicht), and falsified manure transport documents (VDM's) under the Dutch Meststoffenwet regime. Per protocol rules, agricultural manure and phosphate quota/processing disputes are classified as NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

This Dutch CBb decision concerns an administrative fine under the Meststoffenwet (Msw) for exceeding agricultural application standards for animal manure and phosphate, including a dispute over the calculation of opening fertilizer inventory. Under the protocol rules, Meststoffenwet manure/phosphate quota and usage-standard disputes are explicitly classified as NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

The decision directly adjudicates the adoption of a Dutch polder water area management plan (watergebiedsplan) for the Bloemendalerpolder, including water-level regulation measures (flexibel peil, verhoogd peil), an altered drainage route (gewijzigde afvoerroute), and water quality assessment. This falls squarely under substantive water governance (WATER) and specifically waterboard_governance (waterschap peil/watergebiedsplan decisions), with no household service connection refusal or informal settlement issue.

The Dutch Raad van State decision directly concerns a water permit (watervergunning) granted by the regional water authority (Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland) to Schiphol Nederland B.V. authorizing the discharge of substances from a soil depot into a surface water body (polder ditch). This squarely falls under WATER and the regulatory_permit category, with no household service connection or informal settlement dimension.

The Dutch administrative court decision (RBMNE) explicitly adjudicates an appeal concerning the rejection of an application for a water permit ('Afwijzing aanvraag watervergunning'). Under the protocol, disputes over a Dutch watervergunning (Waterwet/waterboard regulatory permit) are substantively WATER under both labels and fall squarely into the regulatory_permit governance category, with no household utility connection refusal or informal settlement issue involved.

Dutch CBb appeal concerning administrative fines in a manure law case (Meststoffenzaak) for improperly determining phosphate and nitrogen content in manure samples, untruthful animal manure transport documents (Vervoersbewijs Dierlijke Meststoffen), and evidentiary requirements for co-perpetration (medeplegen). Under the protocol, agricultural manure/fertilizer regulation cases are NOT_WATER.

The decision concerns an administrative fine for violating the Dutch Fertilizers Act (Meststoffenwet), disputing manure stock accounting, sediment layers, pig phosphate retention from phosphate-rich feed, and fine proportionality. Under the protocol rules, agricultural manure and phosphate regulation disputes under the Meststoffenwet are NOT_WATER.

This CBb decision concerns the revocation of a manure derogation permit and an administrative fine for a minor exceedance of the phosphate application standard by a dairy farmer under the Dutch Meststoffenwet (Fertilizers Act). Under the protocol rules, disputes concerning agricultural manure and phosphate application standards/quotas under the Meststoffenwet are classified as NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

The decision concerns an administrative enforcement request regarding odour nuisance (geuroverlast) emitted into outdoor air via a chimney by a manure-processing and transshipment facility (overslag- en mestverwerkingsbedrijf) in Helmond. It deals with air/odour emissions rather than water law, water resources, or water/sanitation services.

The decision directly adjudicates an appeal against the granting of a water permit (watervergunning) under Chapter 6 of the Dutch Water Act (Waterwet) for (re)building a shed and raising ground within the core protection zone of a regional flood defence (kernzone van een regionale kering), assessing flood safety (waterveiligheid) under the applicable implementation rules. It is squarely a water law regulatory permit dispute and does not involve household water/sanitation connection refusal or informal settlements.

The Dutch Raad van State decision concerns an administrative enforcement order (last onder bestuursdwang) requiring an establishment operator to clean rainwater drainage pits (hemelwaterafvoerputten) and remove grease-laden wastewater (vethoudend afvalwater), directly involving wastewater and stormwater drainage infrastructure governance.

The decision directly adjudicates a challenge to a water permit (watervergunning) for mooring facilities (afmeervoorzieningen) granted by a Dutch regional water board (hoogheemraadschap) under Articles 2.1 and 6.21 of the Dutch Water Act (Waterwet). Because the primary dispute concerns the statutory criteria, conditions, and refusal grounds for a Waterwet permit, it is substantively WATER under both labels and falls squarely within regulatory_permit, with no household connection refusal or informal settlement access issue.

The Dutch CBb decision concerns administrative fines for exceeding the agricultural phosphate application standard (fosfaatgebruiksnorm) and lacking a transport document for animal manure (vervoersbewijs dierlijke meststoffen) under the Meststoffenwet, which is explicitly excluded from water law/governance under the protocol.

This CBb decision concerns an administrative fine imposed under Articles 33a(5) and 59 of the Dutch Meststoffenwet (Fertilizers Act) for failing to fulfil agricultural manure/phosphate processing obligations via a tripartite agreement (DPO) or animal manure transport document (VDM). Under the coding protocol, agricultural manure and phosphate regulatory disputes under the Meststoffenwet are explicitly classified as NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

This Dutch administrative law decision concerns an administrative fine imposed under the Fertilizers Act (Meststoffenwet) regarding classification as an animal manure processor based on tripartite agreements and manure transport documents (Vervoersbewijzen Dierlijke Meststoffen). Under the protocol rules, Meststoffenwet agricultural manure regulation disputes are explicitly classified as NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

This Dutch Raad van State decision reviews a coordinated package of six administrative decisions for the Geertjesgolf project, explicitly including a permit under the Water Act (vergunning krachtens de Waterwet) alongside two spatial zoning plans, an environmental permit, a nature conservation permit, and an excavation permit. Under the protocol, review of a Waterwet permit is substantively WATER under both mananciais_calibrated_label and strict_service_access_label, with regulatory_permit as the primary water-governance category and no household connection or informal-settlement issue.

The decision explicitly adjudicates an appeal concerning a permit issued under the Dutch Water Act (vergunning op grond van de Waterwet), placing it squarely within water law and regulatory permitting under the protocol rules.

The Dutch District Court of Gelderland decision explicitly concerns hydrology and a Water Act project plan ('Projectplan. Waterwet.', the statutory instrument under Art. 5.4 Waterwet used by water authorities/waterboards for constructing or modifying water management works, reviewed with STAB expert advice alongside Art. 8 ECHR and Art. 12(1) ICESCR). It is substantively about systemic water governance under the Waterwet and does not involve household service connection refusal or informal settlements.

This Dutch administrative decision reviews an environmental permit (omgevingsvergunning) for a manure processing facility and upholds the appeals in substantive part because the permit failed to properly assess Best Available Techniques for wastewater (de BBT voor afvalwater), alongside odour policy, EIA screening, and nature-permit assessment. Because industrial/facility wastewater treatment and effluent standards (BBT voor afvalwater) form an explicit substantive ground of judicial annulment rather than an incidental mention or a non-water Meststoffenwet quota dispute, both labels are coded WATER under environmental_protection, with no household connection or informal-settlement issue.

This Dutch administrative court decision (Rechtbank Den Haag) directly adjudicates the protective scope (relativiteitsvereiste / Schutznorm) of the Dutch Water Act (Waterwet), holding that the Waterwet does not serve to protect the interests of the plaintiffs and dismissing the appeal as unfounded. Because the ruling substantively interprets and applies statutory water governance norms under the Waterwet in an administrative appeal, both mananciais_calibrated_label and strict_service_access_label are WATER, categorized under regulatory_permit (Waterwet litigation), with no household service connection refusal or informal settlement issue involved.

The decision directly adjudicates an administrative enforcement order (last onder dwangsom) imposed by the Minister for discharging substances into a surface water body without a required permit or exemption under Article 6.2(1) of the Dutch Waterwet (Water Act). Because the primary dispute concerns unpermitted discharge into surface water under the Waterwet permit/exemption regime, it is substantively WATER under both labels and falls under regulatory_permit, with no household connection refusal or informal settlement issue.

The decision reviews a project plan adopted pursuant to the Dutch Water Act (Projectplan op grond van de Waterwet) by the executive board (het college) regarding waterworks infrastructure and claimants' demand for a concrete sheet pile wall (betonnen damwand). This falls squarely within substantive water governance and specifically waterboard project-plan governance (waterboard_governance), with no household service connection or informal settlement issue.

This Dutch Raad van State decision directly adjudicates a Ministerial water permit (watervergunning under the Waterwet) granted for placing and maintaining a pavilion and associated works in Noord-Beveland, including the permit's temporal duration until 31 December 2030. Under the coding protocol, Waterwet/watervergunning disputes are substantively WATER and fall squarely within regulatory_permit, without involving household water/sanitation connection refusal or informal settlements.

The Dutch Council of State (RvS) decision adjudicates an obligation to tolerate works (gedoogplicht) imposed under Article 5.24(1) of the Waterwet for executing the dike reinforcement project plan ("Waterwet dijkversterking Gorinchem-Waardenburg") along the Waal river and redesigning adjacent floodplains (uiterwaarden), squarely falling under waterboard governance and dike reinforcement project plans.

This Dutch administrative decision reviews an environmental permit (omgevingsvergunning) and EIA screening (MER-beoordeling) for a manure-processing facility, holding that the authority failed to adequately assess significant adverse environmental impacts regarding energy efficiency and micropollutants in the facility's wastewater (afvalwater)—specifically pesticides, antibiotics, growth promoters, pharmaceutical residues, and endocrine-disrupting substances. Because wastewater effluent contamination is a direct, dispositive ground of judicial review rather than an incidental mention or a non-water Meststoffenwet quota dispute, both labels are WATER and the primary governance category is environmental_protection (industrial effluent pollution).

The decision concerns a general environmental permit, EIA screening, Natura-2000 assessment, air emissions, and odour nuisance for the expansion of a biogas production plant in Luttelgeest. Although one brief sentence notes that there is sufficient clarity regarding what happens with wastewater ('afvalwater'), this mention is purely incidental to a broader industrial/energy environmental permit dispute rather than substantive water law, water governance, or wastewater infrastructure adjudication.

This Raad van State decision concerns municipal enforcement (last onder dwangsom) under Articles 6 and 13 of the Dutch Soil Protection Act (Wet bodembescherming) requiring a soil investigation (inventariserend bodemonderzoek) and soil remediation after an agricultural enterprise discharged crop protection chemicals directly onto soil (geloosd op de bodem / bodemlozingen). The dispute governs terrestrial soil contamination rather than water law, water resources, or water/sanitation services.

The Raad van State decision concerns a water permit (watervergunning) granted by a regional water authority (Hoogheemraadschap) for performing activities in a water system (watersysteem), placing it squarely within water law/governance under regulatory_permit.

The decision adjudicates custom regulatory prescriptions (maatwerkvoorschriften) for a discharge (lozing) under the Dutch Decree on Discharges Outside Establishments (Besluit lozen buiten inrichtingen, Blbi), specifically reviewing the environmental impact assessment of the discharge and annulling a stricter custom emission limit for pentachlorophenol (PCP) above the exhaustive 20 micrograms per liter standard in Article 3.1(2) Blbi. Because the primary dispute concerns administrative authority and conditions governing a regulated liquid/wastewater discharge, it is substantively WATER under both labels and falls under regulatory_permit, without involving household connection refusal or informal settlements.

The decision concerns an environmental permit (omgevingsvergunning) for the temporary construction and operation of a wastewater treatment plant (zuiveringsinstallatie) designed to reduce toluene concentrations in industrial wastewater generated during oil extraction in Schoonebeek prior to subsurface injection in Twente, and whether an environmental foundation opposing wastewater injection has standing (belanghebbende). Because it directly adjudicates permitting for industrial wastewater treatment infrastructure and effluent pollution control, it is substantively WATER under both labels and best fits environmental_protection.

The Dutch Council of State (RvS) decision concerns a refusal to take enforcement action regarding an alleged breach of conditions attached to a water permit (watervergunning). Enforcement of watervergunning conditions falls squarely within water governance and the regulatory_permit category, without involving household water/sanitation connection refusal or informal settlements.

The decision concerns an administrative fine under the Dutch Fertilizers Act (Meststoffenwet) for exceeding application standards for animal manure and nitrogen, along with arguments regarding nitrogen volatilization corrections and flat-rate nitrogen/phosphate stock levels. Under the protocol rules, agricultural manure/nitrogen/phosphate regulation under the Meststoffenwet without water law or water governance adjudication is classified as NOT_WATER.

This CBb decision concerns agricultural phosphate quotas (fosfaatrechten), land-boundedness (grondgebondenheid), cross-border agricultural parcels in Belgium (Grensboerregeling) under the Dutch Meststoffenwet (Msw), and dairy cattle expansion limits under the Natuurbeschermingswet 1998. Under the coding protocol, Meststoffenwet manure/phosphate quota disputes are explicitly NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

The Dutch Council of State (RvS) decision concerns the amendment by the executive board (dagelijks bestuur) of a water permit (watervergunning) for discharging effluent from Sitech's integrated wastewater treatment plant (IAZI). Wastewater discharge licensing under a watervergunning falls squarely within WATER and the regulatory_permit category.

This Dutch administrative law decision (Rechtbank Den Haag) concerns a municipal enforcement order subject to periodic penalty payments (last onder dwangsom) issued by the Municipality of Westland regarding the discharge of urban wastewater (lozen van stedelijk afvalwater), evaluating proportionality, penalty amount, and compliance period. Because the dispute directly governs urban wastewater/sewage discharge regulation and enforcement, both labels are WATER and the primary governance category is sanitation_sewage.

The Dutch Council of State (RvS) decision directly adjudicates a Ministerial project plan ("Zandsuppletie Roggenplaat" / sand nourishment on the Roggenplaat shoal) adopted pursuant to Article 5.4 of the Waterwet (Dutch Water Act), which governs the construction and modification of water management works (waterstaatswerken) in waterways/coastal waters. It is substantively about systemic water governance under both primary labels and does not involve household service connections or informal settlements.

The Dutch District Court Noord-Holland decision explicitly concerns permitting under the Water Act (Waterwet) and Water Decree (Waterbesluit) for an open aquifer thermal energy storage / groundwater abstraction-infiltration system (open bodemenergiesysteem), specifically addressing whether multiple permits can be granted for the same location. This squarely falls under WATER and regulatory_permit, with no household utility connection refusal or informal settlement involvement.

The decision directly adjudicates an appeal against a permit issued under the Dutch Water Act (vergunning op grond van de Waterwet) for activities related to new housing construction, annulling the decision insofar as it lacked a permit condition requiring prior water compensation before filling in (demping) 120 m2 of surface water. This squarely constitutes a water law regulatory permit dispute (WATER / regulatory_permit) and does not involve household service connection refusal or informal settlement water access.

The Dutch Raad van State decision directly concerns a ministerial decision adopting the river management project plan "Stroomlijn Nederrijn en Lek spoor 4" under Article 5.4(1) of the Water Act (Waterwet) for the Nederrijn and Lek waterways. It is substantively about public-law water and river/waterway governance under both label standards and does not involve household service connections or informal settlements.

The decision concerns custom environmental prescriptions (maatwerkvoorschriften) imposed by provincial authorities on a manure/fertilizer pellet production and storage facility due to odour nuisance (geurhinder), which falls squarely outside water law and water governance.

The Dutch administrative court decision directly adjudicates a challenge to a water permit (watervergunning) for mooring facilities under Articles 2.1 and 6.21 of the Dutch Water Act (Waterwet). Under the protocol, Waterwet/watervergunning adjudication is substantively WATER and falls squarely under regulatory_permit, with no household utility connection or informal settlement issue.

This Dutch Council of State (RvS) decision concerns a municipal zoning plan (bestemmingsplan) and coordinated permits—explicitly including a Ministerial water permit (watervergunning)—for sand/clay extraction and redevelopment of the Waal river floodplains (uiterwaarden) in the Willemspolder to improve high-water flood safety (hoogwaterveiligheid) and nature development. It directly involves water governance, floodplain spatial planning, and a Waterwet permit, without involving household water/sanitation connection refusal or informal settlements.

The Dutch District Court of The Hague (RBDHA) decision concerns an administrative enforcement order (last onder dwangsom) for repeatedly discharging wastewater (lozen van afvalwater) from storing non-inert goods (Activiteitenbesluit § 3.4.3) that allegedly exceeded the sulphate concentration limit prescribed in an environmental permit (omgevingsvergunning). Wastewater discharge regulation and effluent pollution enforcement fall squarely within WATER under both protocol labels, with primary category environmental_protection (industrial/commercial effluent pollution enforcement under permit/Activiteitenbesluit rules) and no household connection refusal or informal settlement issue.

The Dutch court summary explicitly identifies the case as an oral judgment ('mondelinge uitspraak') under the Dutch Water Act ('Waterwet'), establishing that the dispute substantively concerns statutory water law/governance, though the brief summary does not specify the exact sub-type of Waterwet decision (e.g., permit, enforcement, or compensation), warranting 'other_water'.

The decision of the Dutch Council of State (RvS) directly concerns a water permit (watervergunning) granted to Stichting RiF010 for developing a water sports facility in an urban waterway (Binnenrotte/Steigersgracht) and within the protection zones of an adjacent flood-defence embankment (boezemwaterkering) in Rotterdam. Under the protocol, disputes over a Dutch watervergunning and flood-defence protection zones are substantively WATER under both labels and map to regulatory_permit, with no household utility connection refusal or informal settlement involvement.

The preliminary relief ruling directly concerns Dutch water governance and permitting: an enforcement request regarding works carried out by PWN in coastal dune water-defence protection zones (kernzone, beschermingszone A, and beschermingszone B) without a required water permit (watervergunning) under Article 3.2 of the Keur Hoogheemraadschap Hollands Noorderkwartier 2016, and the subsequent legalization of those works via a granted watervergunning. It does not involve household service connection refusal or informal settlements.

The Rotterdam District Court decision explicitly adjudicates an administrative enforcement request (handhavingsverzoek) under the Dutch Water Act (Waterwet), confirming that the respondent authority rightly rejected the claimant's request for enforcement. Because the dispute directly concerns regulatory enforcement under the Waterwet, both primary labels are WATER and it falls under regulatory_permit, with no household connection refusal or informal settlement issue.

The CBb decision concerns an administrative fine imposed under the Dutch Fertilizers Act (Meststoffenwet) for exceeding animal manure application standards based on invalid manure transport documents (VDMs). Under the protocol rules, agricultural manure regulations under the Meststoffenwet are explicitly classified as NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

The decision concerns administrative fines under Articles 53, 55 and 56 of the Dutch Uitvoeringsregeling Meststoffenwet (Fertilisers Act implementation regulation) for failing to properly record solid manure transport data via GPS/automatic data registration equipment and inaccurately completing animal manure transport documents (VDM). Under the protocol rules, disputes under the Dutch Meststoffenwet regarding agricultural manure regulation are classified as NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

The Dutch Council of State (RvS) decision concerns an administrative enforcement order (last onder dwangsom) requiring a facility (Orion) in Drachten to cease discharging polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB)-containing wastewater (afvalwater). Because the dispute directly adjudicates industrial effluent/wastewater pollution control and wastewater discharge enforcement, both water labels are WATER and the primary governance category is environmental_protection.

The decision concerns an appeal against a waterboard decision under the Dutch Waterwet and Waterschapswet partially revising the register of surface water bodies (legger oppervlaktewaterlichamen) in Geertruidenberg, which directly falls under systemic waterboard governance (WATER).

The decision concerns an administrative dispute under Article 3.131 of the Dutch Activiteitenbesluit regarding the municipal executive's refusal to grant a custom prescription (maatwerkvoorschrift) allowing a catering establishment (horecazaak) to discharge grease-containing wastewater (vethoudend afvalwater) without first routing it through a grease separator (vetafscheider). Because it directly adjudicates commercial wastewater discharge rules and grease-trap requirements protecting wastewater/sewer infrastructure, both `mananciais_calibrated_label` and `strict_service_access_label` are `WATER`, the primary category is `sanitation_sewage` (closely intersecting with regulatory wastewater discharge governance), and it does not involve a utility connection refusal or informal settlement.

The Dutch Raad van State decision concerns an administrative dispute (timeliness and rejection of a Wet openbaarheid van bestuur disclosure request) against a regional water authority (Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland) specifically seeking non-public records on the hydrological impacts (waterafvoer and watercompensatie) of constructing a Multifunctional Accommodation in Zwammerdam. Institutional transparency and accountability of a Dutch water board over water drainage and water compensation fall within water governance (waterboard_governance), though confidence is marked medium because the procedural vehicle is an FOI (Wob) request rather than a direct substantive Waterwet/keur permit review.

Dutch CBb decision concerning Common Agricultural Policy (GLB) cross-compliance (randvoorwaarden) and an alleged violation of Article 8a of the Besluit gebruik meststoffen (Decree on the Use of Fertilizers/Manure), along with evidentiary and procedural hearing requirements. Agricultural fertilizer/manure compliance disputes are not substantively water law or water governance.

The decision of the Dutch Trade and Industry Appeals Tribunal (CBb) concerns an administrative fine under the Dutch Fertilizers Act (Meststoffenwet) for exceeding animal manure and nitrogen application standards, as well as evidentiary disputes over manure removal and inventory reporting. Under the protocol, agricultural manure/nitrogen disputes under the Meststoffenwet are explicitly NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

The decision of the Dutch Raad van State concerns an administrative project plan ("Kadeverlaging Scherpekamp" — embankment lowering) adopted by the Minister as water manager pursuant to Article 5.4 of the Dutch Waterwet for modifying water management/flood-defence infrastructure (waterstaatswerk). It clearly falls within substantive water law and public water-authority infrastructure project-plan governance, with no household connection refusal or informal settlement issue.

This Dutch Trade and Industry Appeals Tribunal (CBb) decision concerns administrative fines and a 5% cross-compliance reduction (randvoorwaardenkorting) imposed under the Dutch Fertilizers Act (Meststoffenwet) for exceeding manure application standards (gebruiksnormen), failing to meet manure processing obligations (mestverwerkingsplichten), and falsifying Animal Manure Transport Documents (Vervoersbewijzen Dierlijke Meststoffen). Under the coding protocol, Dutch Meststoffenwet manure/fertilizer compliance disputes are explicitly NOT_WATER and not_water_related.

The Dutch Raad van State decision adjudicates the refusal by the regional water authority (Hoogheemraadschap Amstel, Gooi en Vecht) to grant a water permit (watervergunning) for soil remediation, raising ground elevation in a boezem water-storage area, filling indirect water storage, digging four boat slips (insteekhavens), and installing bank revetments in connection with residential construction. This squarely falls under WATER and regulatory_permit, without involving household water/sanitation connection refusal or informal settlements.

This CBb decision concerns a 20% Common Agricultural Policy cross-compliance subsidy reduction (randvoorwaardenkorting under Regulation 1306/2013) imposed on a farmer for failing to apply manure using low-emission methods under Dutch manure-use regulations (Besluit gebruik meststoffen and Uitvoeringsregeling gebruik meststoffen). Although Annex II cross-references the Nitrates Directive, the primary dispute concerns agricultural subsidy compliance and manure-spreading rules rather than water law, water infrastructure, or water governance.
